children: For instance, Micron Technology Inc. (MU, Financials) makes memory chips for AI and data-center applications, offering DRAM and high-bandwidth memory, and it is confronting a new competitive development out of China.

ChangXin Memory Technologies, or CXMT, has begun mass production of its fifth-generation DRAM platform, which it says can yield at least 50% more dies per wafer than its previous iteration. CXMT has announced two 24-gigabit LPDDR5X processors for cellphones and other portable devices .

The advancement may put pressure on Micron and SK Hynix in conventional DRAM. According to TrendForce, CXMT had 9.5% of worldwide DRAM revenue in the second quarter of 2026, compared to 23.3% for Micron and 24.9% for SK Hynix.

The overlap between the two seems minimal for now. CXMT's recent products are mostly targeted at mobile and traditional DRAM, whereas Micron and SK Hynix have been transitioning more capacity to HBM and high-capacity server memory utilized in artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
And that distinction counts. If CXMT moves beyond mobile DRAM into server memory and more advanced products, that would pose a bigger risk to the two firms.
According to TipRanks, analysts see upside potential of 54.01% for Micron and 33.17% for SK Hynix, reflecting continued bullish sentiment on Wall Street for both stocks.
The next question for investors is whether CXMT can translate better wafer efficiency into a wider challenge to the global memory giants.

title: China's Memory Push Raises a New Question for Micron and SK Hynix
